newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes lower, pessimism reigns.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes lower, pessimism reigns.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index fell again on Tuesday as the current mood of gloom about the country's economic prospects continued to push major issues lower.

Analysts said equities markets throughout the region were all being hit by bearish sentiment but added that the Czech market was likely to underperform its neighbours because of relatively weak economic fundamentals.
"I think the Czech market will again be the one being hurt the most. I'm rather negative," said Eugene Klerk of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
Klerk said that the government's recent package of measures designed to stimulate growth had failed to revive optimism because of the central bank's continued tight grip on monetary policy.
"The central bank is independent and it has the key bvuttons in terms of ineterest rates. So the government can't do much," he said.
The major issue decliners were led by CEZ which fell 31 crowns to 970 and Komercni Banka which lost 30 crowns to 2,220.
